title: Most people think the cross was the final moment.
paragraphs: Most people think the cross was the final moment.
It wasn’t.
Something else happened… quietly, violently, and almost hidden from public view.
Inside the temple—far from the crowds, far from the noise of Golgotha—there stood a veil.

Massive.
Heavy.
Sacred.
It wasn’t just fabric.
It was a boundary.
This veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place—the very dwelling place of God’s presence (Exodus 26:33).
No one walked in there casually.
No one wandered in out of curiosity.

Only the high priest could enter.
Once a year.
With blood.
And even then, not without fear (Hebrews 9:7).
Because that veil was a message:
“God is holy… and you are not.”
Now imagine the moment.
Jesus is hanging on the cross.

His body is torn.
His breath is fading.
The sky grows dark.
And then—He cries out…
“It is finished.” (John 19:30)
And He gives up His spirit.
At that exact moment…
The veil tears.

Not slowly.
Not symbolically.
Not from the bottom—like a human would do.
From top… to bottom. (Matthew 27:51)
God did it.
This wasn’t just a miracle.
It was an announcement.
Heaven was declaring something that would redefine humanity’s relationship with God forever.
Here’s the truth most people miss:
The veil didn’t exist to keep people from God…
It existed to protect people from His holiness.
Because sin and holiness cannot coexist.
So the veil stood as both a barrier and a mercy.
But when Jesus died, everything changed.
Because the cross didn’t just deal with sin…
It satisfied justice.
It fulfilled the law.
It completed the requirement for atonement once and for all (Hebrews 10:12).
And so the veil was no longer needed.
Not because God became less holy…
But because through Christ, we can now stand before Him.
Let that sink in.

The place that once required fear…
Now invites intimacy.

The presence that once demanded distance…
Now welcomes you near.
But here’s where it gets personal.
Many people today still live like the veil is intact.

They pray like God is far.
They worship like they’re unworthy to come close.
They carry guilt that Jesus already paid for.

They stand outside…
Even though the door is gone.
The veil didn’t tear halfway.
God didn’t say, “Come closer… but not too close.”
He tore it completely.
Access wasn’t partially granted.
It was fully opened.
But access doesn’t mean casual.
This is where we must be careful.
The tearing of the veil was free for us…
But it was not cheap.
It cost the blood of Jesus.
So yes—you can come boldly (Hebrews 4:16).
But never carelessly.
Because the same God who invites you in…
Is still holy.
Here’s the deeper lesson:

Jesus didn’t just open a way…
He became the way. (John 14:6)
There is no longer a curtain.
There is no longer a system of barriers.
There is no longer a human mediator standing between you and God.
Christ is your access.
Christ is your covering.
Christ is your High Priest.
And this changes everything about how you live.

You don’t pray to be heard—you’re already invited.
You don’t worship to earn presence—you’re already in it.
You don’t strive for acceptance—you already have it in Christ.
But the real question is not:
“Did the veil tear?”
It did.
The real question is:
Why are you still standing outside?
Why live distant when access has been granted?
Why carry shame when forgiveness has been completed?
Why act like God is unreachable…
When He is now near?
Some people are waiting for a sign.
The veil was the sign.
Some people are waiting to feel worthy.
Jesus made you worthy through His sacrifice.
So stop knocking on a door that no longer exists.
Step in.
Draw near.
Live like the veil is truly gone.
Because it is.

“The veil was torn, but many still live separated.”
“Access to God is not earned—it was given through sacrifice.”
“You are not standing outside because you’re unworthy… but because you haven’t stepped in.”
The cross didn’t just forgive you.
It brought you close.

Engagement Question:
Do you truly live like you have direct access to God—or do you still feel like you’re standing outside the veil?
